customManagers.description: The OTP and Elixir versions the Elixir CI matrix runs on are workflow_call input defaults, which the github-actions manager does not see -- it reads `uses:` references only. Left unmanaged they simply rot: the LTS OTP pin sat twelve patch releases behind before anyone noticed (#146). Each default carries a `# renovate:` annotation naming its upstream, and this manager turns the pair into a dependency. Every key is written out on every annotation rather than made optional, so that the pattern has no optional groups to leave empty.

packageRules.description: Keep the html-validation Python runtime pinned (3.11 was chosen deliberately). A new Python minor may lack html5validator / tool support and CI does not exercise it here, so bump it manually rather than via the grouped auto-merge.

texlive-ja-textlint uses a custom YYYY[revision-letter] tag scheme (e.g. 2025g, 2026a). The default docker versioning mis-orders it (it treated bare 2025 as newer than 2025g). Use loose versioning and restrict candidates to plain year tags so Renovate orders them correctly and ignores the alpine/debian/amd64/test/latest variants.

OTP tags a maintenance release with a fourth component (27.3.4.16), which is not semver, hence loose versioning. Loose does not recognise a pre-release either, so restrict candidates to all-numeric versions and leave the rc tags out.

The two rows of the CI matrix are a supported older pair and the newest pair, so the older row has to stay on its line: without this it would be offered OTP 29 and stop being the thing it is there to test. Moving the row to the next line is a decision to make deliberately, by editing this range.
The Elixir half of the same older pair. See the erlang/otp-lts rule above.
